title: Sprint-level capacity buffering & budget cascade
summary: Working workbook for translating 12-week product sprints into a budget cascade that includes a sprint-level capacity buffer (GPU-hours and contingency FTEs), run-rate implications, and pricing sensitivity to token demand and per-token revenue. Intended as a decision support artifact for Finance + Product to set hiring/capacity trigger rules and temporary reserve buckets.
purpose: Provide an operationally actionable budget view mapping sprint deliverables (feature launches, promoted experiments) to incremental capacity needs and headcount/phased hiring. Output: recommended sprint buffer policy, near-term hiring freeze triggers, and price/commitment levers to manage unit economics under demand shocks.
assumptions: Baseline month = March 2026. Baseline demand = 1.2B tokens/mo (avg across hosted customers). Baseline model mix: 60% base-gen (small-medium models), 30% instruction-tuned medium, 10% large family (high-cost tails). Baseline infra cost per GPU-hour = $2.80 (weighted spot+reserved mix). Average response length = 75 tokens. People fully loaded cost per FTE (ENG/SRE/OPS) = $18k/mo. Hiring lead time = 8 weeks for senior infra, 6 weeks for mid-level engineers. Buffer policy target = 15% GPU-hour headroom + 1.5 contingency FTEs per 20 engineers.
scenarios: SCENARIO A (Base): tokens +0% run-rate. No new hires except committed. SCENARIO B (Acceleration): tokens +25% over 12 weeks driven by 2 enterprise expansions; require +40% GPU-hours, add 3 short-term contractors or shift burst capacity. SCENARIO C (Demand Shock): tokens -30% (customers throttle); evaluate furlough/hiring freeze and temporary spot reductions. SCENARIO D (Price Compression): per-token revenue -20% due to competitive pressure; model effect on margin and runway. SCENARIO E (Cost Shock): GPU-hour cost +30% (regional capacity premium); evaluate tradeoff: raise prices vs. use quantized lower-cost model variants.
headcount_plan:
Sprint-level hires (12-week window):
- Infra (serving/runtime): current 14 FTE -> plan add 2 hires Y1Q2 (starts wk3) -> contingency +1 contractor for spikes (6-8 week contract)
- SRE/ops: current 8 FTE -> plan add 1 (on-call rotation coverage) -> contingency +0.5 FTE via overtime/budgeted contractor
- Product/Platform: current 10 FTE -> no hires in window; re-prioritize feature owners to cut nonessential work if demand shock
- Solutions (customer success escalations): +1 temporary SE on 12-week contract for two large deals in scenario B
Cost assumptions per role (monthly fully loaded):
- Infra eng: $20,000
- SRE: $17,500
- Product PM/PD: $16,000
- Solutions SE (contract): $13,000/month
Recruiting lead-time risk: if tokens accelerate in <8 weeks, prefer contractors or reserved-burst purchase instead of permanent hires.
budget_breakdown:
12-week cascade (high level, $000s)
- People (ops+eng+product): baseline 12-week run-rate = $1,350k
- Infra (GPU cloud + reserved commitments): baseline 12-week = $720k
- Reserved burst & spot buffer bucket (target 15% of infra spend): $108k
- Third-party tooling & observability: $48k
- Contingency hiring pool (contractor budget): $120k
- Total baseline 12-week budget: $2,346k
Incremental (scenario B acceleration): +GPU-hours cost $288k, +contractor/se solutions $52k, net 12-week = $2,686k
Downside (scenario C demand shock): infra variable down -$216k, but fixed reserved commitments still burn $360k -> net -$96k; headcount reductions yield savings only after 6-8 weeks.
sensitivity_analysis:
Inputs varied across three levers: token demand (+/- 10/25/40%), per-token revenue (-20/-10/+10), GPU-hour cost (+15/+30). Key outputs tracked: 12-week gross margin delta, cash burn delta, trigger points for hiring freeze, and break-even committed price per 1M tokens for target margin.
SELECTED RESULTS (rounded):
- +25% tokens (Scenario B): incremental infra spend +40% -> gross margin down 4 ppt vs base unless partial pass-through or model mix shifts to cheaper variants. Cash burn increases by ~$340k over 12 weeks.
- -30% tokens (Scenario C): infra variable drops by ~30% but fixed reserved cost mean margins compress 6 ppt; runway improves by ~2.2 months only if we implement hiring freeze + pause reserved expansion.
- GPU-cost +30%: without price adjust, margin compresses 5-7 ppt; with 10% product price increase, margin impact neutralized but increases churn risk (estimate ~2-3% churn uplift).
Break-even revenue per 1M tokens (Base mix): $220-$260 depending on pass-through of infra buffer and whether dedicated committed discounts applied.
recommended_actions:
1) Approve sprint buffer policy: maintain 15% GPU-hour reserve and a $120k 12-week contractor pool; review monthly.
2) Trigger rules: if run-rate token growth >18% over 2 consecutive weeks -> authorize immediate $100k burst-reserve purchase and open 2 contract roles.
3) Hiring: delay permanent infra hires until wk6 of accelerated demand; prefer contractors for short lead-time.
4) Pricing levers: prepare a 10% near-term price protection plan for large customers and a comms playbook to negotiate incremental committed capacity at discount vs on-demand.
5) Cost mitigation: accelerate deployment of quantized-medium model variant for high-volume customers to reduce per-token infra by ~12%.
6) Finance ops: add a sprint-level dashboard (weekly) to monitor token velocity, GPU-hour utilization, reserved vs on-demand split, and projected 12-week burn.
7) Executive: re-evaluate reserved capacity buys each 4 weeks vs spot availability following GPU price indices.
risks:
- Timing mismatch: hiring lead times longer than demand accelerations -> reliance on costly contractors or burst purchases.
- Fixed commitments: reserved capacity commitments create cash drag during demand dips.
- Churn risk: price increases to offset GPU-cost shocks can drive customers to competitors.
- Model migration risk: moving customers to cheaper model variants may degrade quality and increase support overhead.
- Macro GPU price volatility: sudden regional spot squeezes could exceed buffer policy and force emergency purchases.
